projectOverrides.why: Every research and implementation task on EDI itself runs on Opus 5.5 at high effort: nothing more, nothing less.

categories.when: Research, design, specification, plans and story breakdowns, investigation of an unknown cause, audits and reproduction.
categories.why: A wrong plan or diagnosis costs a whole implementation round.

categories.when: Features and stories, refactors and structural sweeps, backend and frontend, with a settled plan from a research task.
categories.why: The hard reasoning is already written down in the plan; high effort because the change must be right first time.

categories.when: The same work when no settled plan exists, such as full-stack stories and broad sweeps.
categories.why: The worker holds domain rules, layers and acceptance criteria at once, with no plan to lean on.

categories.when: A defect whose cause is established by a report, a stack trace naming the fault, or the captain; an unknown cause is research first.
categories.why: The cause is known, and the regression test must be right first time.

categories.when: Prose documentation, decision records and story text in a repository.
categories.why: Well-defined formats that a reviewer reads in full.

categories.when: CI/CD and pipeline changes, builds and deployments, dependency upgrades, tracker operations, developer tooling and onboarding scripts.
categories.why: Failures here have been non-obvious, such as proxies, DNS and wrong remotes, so medium rather than low.

categories.when: A single obvious outcome a reviewer verifies at a glance: a rename with a known target, a formatting sweep, a typo, a one-value configuration change.
categories.why: The token saver, made foolproof: the brief names the exact change and files, and the done is checked before it is accepted.

categories.when: A small change request on a branch already delivered, under about fifty lines, with the design settled.
categories.why: A fresh worker fixes the one thing without paying again for a long earlier context.
